doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: Jazz Griots film idea, Madrid with Sara Baras, and asking for what you want
summary: Ries describes the film project documenting African-American musicians, then taking an impromptu trip to Madrid to perform with flamenco dancer Sara Baras.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: they’re just like being nice. Turns out he was being nice and he got back to New York, sure enough I met with this director Jordan Walker-Pearlman. He goes, “I hear you have ideas for movies.” And I actually took out a list of like ten ideas. And he looks at these ideas and he goes, “I think we should do that one first, what do you think?” I said, “Yeah.” He goes, “Okay let’s start.” And believe it or not we filmed already two and then right before the pandemic so we’re trying to now start again. But it’s my idea that African-American culture, music, has to be recognized as how brilliant it actually is rather than you know like films that are made about jazz the concept is you know, oh drugs and alcohol. You know it’s like, rather than wait a minute — to play music to that level like Elvin Jones or Jack DeJohnette or Miles Davis or Wayne Shorter or Duke Ellington, you have to be unbelievably brilliant to be able to play at that level that brilliantly. And I want white people to know how brilliant they are. So in their own words like the filming of the music but then also capturing them talking about music, their life, so that documentation of these musicians are still alive and we lost a lot of when Jimmy Heath died and Barry Harris — a lot of musicians that we were trying to get passed away so we’re running against the clock a little bit. Sorry that was so long but you know so, yeah, all these projects are great, and the flamenco. In fact because I was in Lisbon with this fado singer Ana Moura we had just finished that recording that I talk about and I saw that Sara Baras, the famous dancer that’s on my recording film, I saw that she was performing in Madrid and they were like, “Let’s go.” So at like one o’clock in the morning we left Lisbon and drove to Madrid all night. We arrived at like seven o’clock in the morning, went to this friend’s house and we just hung out and then I was going to go see Sara, this was a Thursday night or whatever. They were playing for a week there. As it turns out then I stayed in Madrid Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, then I started hanging out. They invited me onstage then I performed Thursday night with them, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. That began my association because of that connection like taking an opportunity like I’m not going to miss out on recording with Elvin — I missed that but I’m not going to miss — I’m taking every opportunity I can to do the things that I want to do while I’m still here.

Yeah. It’s like if you want to do something just do it. So then I realized hey, you know what? The worst thing somebody could say is no. Like okay, I asked. But maybe doesn’t mean no, maybe it just means no right now but maybe in two months it could be a yes, or maybe — but most people said yes. So if you ask —
